status: provisional apparatus outline, not a task or instruction
units: Same reduced epsilon0=mu0=c=1 units as r2. Frequency and momentum relaxation have inverse-time units; thickness is length; nu is length squared/time; alpha=kappa/(m*n0) is length/time; tau=kappa/k_s is time.
public_facts: A homogeneous incompressible Newtonian charged fluid fills 0<z<d between stationary planar substrates, with vacuum optical media outside. Its neutralizing background is fixed. Use the same gamma=.06, nu=.04 and plasma-frequency definition p squared=n0*q squared/m. Linear transverse momentum balance and Maxwell equations define the fields; all other material polarization and surface conductivity are absent.

Each face carries a massless, optically inert tangential layer whose spring and dashpot are in series and anchored to the substrate. Fluid slip velocity is the rate of spring extension plus dashpot velocity; common traction is k_s times extension and kappa times dashpot velocity. The layer has known alpha=kappa/(m*n0) and tau=kappa/k_s, identical at the two faces. Traction opposes slip, and the usual tangential Maxwell boundary conditions hold. The layer adds no normal motion or pressure force to the transverse problem.

The normally incident electric field at the front face is Re[E0 exp(-i*frequency*t)] along y. There is no wave incoming from the rear. Take periodic stationarity before the weak-field limit E0→0. Normal incidence makes wall phase uniform.

A calibrated front-layer thermostat measures removed thermal heat per unit area. It collects heat generated in the dashpot; the spring is an energetic temperature-independent element with no thermal entropy. The thermostat keeps the layer temperature fixed and has negligible response time at the measurement frequencies. Thermal feedback and transport do not affect the leading fields; equilibrium background is subtracted. Bulk fluid/background thermostats are separate.

Divide the measured periodic heat signal by the mean incident optical power. The mean selector returns its cycle average. The in_phase selector returns twice its cycle average against cos(2*frequency*t), and the quadrature selector returns twice its cycle average against sin(2*frequency*t), using the stated incident-field clock. The single common fitted quantity is plasma_frequency; all inputs and material ratios are exact.
private_calibration_intent: Several nonzero finite-relaxation mean-heat settings; both physical and supplied work-attribution predictors share the exact periodic average. No dataset or fixed sigma selected yet.
